Pace (exit 0); subtitles within reading speed. data-read="subtitle"|"label" and data-pace="…" mark clips

commands.name: render
commands.summary: An MP4 drawn through the page contract in one-GOP chunks across several browsers; resumable; each render a version in a project.
commands.when: drafts and the final film of a page-engine project (HyperFrames renders with npx hyperframes render)
reads: <project> or <page.html>, and the files it loads
<project>/REVIEW.md, DECISIONS.md (gate ① on record, for a whole film)
writes: <project>/out/<page>.mp4 (or --out) and <out>.render.json (with files: every file in the page's folder the page loaded, and its sha256)

text: an MP4 drawn through the page contract (the canvas engine, ClaudeAnimationBase, any page that writes
window.film): one-GOP chunks that the --workers browsers take in turn, each into its own x264, BT.709 tv
range, a keyframe every --gop frames, <out>.render.json records how (and every file the page loaded, for
bin/vh assets check); video only (sound: mux). Stopped or
failed, the finished chunks stay: the same command resumes while the page, its files and the options are
unchanged. Over 600 frames it first draws a few and prints the time, size and disk the render needs
(refused when the disk cannot hold it; --no-estimate skips). Says when --fps is not the page's own
(window.film.fps). A relative --out is from the current folder. HyperFrames: npx hyperframes render
(--force to render it here anyway).
A whole standard or studio film waits for gate ① on record (tools/gatecheck.py); --range and --frames do not.
In a project each render is a version (bin/vh versions): the film it replaces is kept in out/versions/

commands.name: patch
commands.summary: Draw frames a–b of a bin/vh render film again and put them back, the rest untouched and checked; by frames, seconds, shot or chapter.
commands.when: a small fix in a long film
reads: <project>/shots.json, or the page's shots and chapters

usage.synopsis: patch <film.mp4> (--frames a-b | --seconds s-e | --shot S04,S05 | --chapter c2)… [--sidecar f.render.json] [--out f | --in-place] [--workers 4] [--frame-timeout 120] [--verify seams|full] [--note text]
text: draw frames a–b of a bin/vh render film again and put them back, the rest untouched: cut on its keyframes
(its .render.json says how it was made), joined, sound and subtitles kept; checks the frame count, that every
packet and pixel outside is the film's, decoding, and that the frames drawn again outside a–b came back the same
(exit 1: the new film is kept as <film>.failed.mp4, or .failed-2.mp4 … when that is there, the film untouched);
without --out: <film>.patched.mp4.
--shot / --chapter: their frames from shots.json or the page's window.film.shots / chapters (through the
next cut's transition); lists and mixes are the union. In a project the result is a version (bin/vh versions)

commands.name: versions
commands.summary: Every film render and patch made in a project, one version each; compare two at a time t, or make an earlier one current again.
commands.when: comparing a fix with the film before it, or going back

usage.synopsis: versions <project> [--json] | versions compare <project> <vA> <vB> --t <s> [--wipe [0.5]] [--out f.png] [--json] | versions use <project> <vN>
text: every film render and patch made there, one version each (out/versions/versions.json: when, the
file, how it was made, what it follows, the spans and shots changed, its check); compare: the
frame at --t of two versions side by side or as a wipe PNG, with the PSNR (from the encoded films);
use: an earlier version is the current film again, the one there now kept (tools/versions.py)

subcommands.name: compare
subcommands.summary: two versions' frame at t, side by side or as a wipe, with the PSNR

subcommands.name: use
subcommands.summary: an earlier version is the current film again

commands.name: check
commands.summary: Check a rendered video: the probe, the BRIEF's spec, gate ① on record, black, freeze and silence, isolated frames, motion, subtitles, colour tags, loudness and the publishing copy; --against a 1080p cut.
commands.when: on every draft, and once before release (CLAUDE.md's floors)

text: ffprobe + the BRIEF's spec (size, rate, length; exit 1 on a mismatch) + gate ①
on record in a standard or studio project (REVIEW.md, DECISIONS.md; exit 1 without it) + the
publishing copy in PACKAGING.md against the platforms' length limits (a warning) +
subtitles (its tracks and the .srt beside it) shorter than it takes to read them (a warning) +
black/freeze/silence detection + isolated-frame scan (one-frame capture glitches; exit 1 on any not
confirmed in the project's confirmed.json (a designed flash: why, evidence, and the key the scan prints,
which lapses when the picture there changes) nor declared for this run with --allow <seconds or spans a-b>;
evenly spaced ones are periodic motion, said, not failed) + motion (hard cuts from dark to bright, still stretches of 3 s or more: warnings) + colour tags

+ loudness (integrated and true peak of the film's sound against what it was mixed to: the project's mix record, else the BRIEF, else −14 LUFS ±1; ≤ −1 dBTP: a warning); --against: a 4K render vs the approved 1080p cut
(exit 1 when the picture differs: a layout that breaks at device scale 2). The result is kept in the
video's project as out/check/<name>.check.json (bin/vh status reads the last; with the video's size and
mtime_ns as the checks began, so a film put back later with an old modification time, or in its place
meanwhile, is told from the one checked); --json prints it instead
of the lines above (those go to stderr): each finding's kind, severity, time and frame, message,
evidence and whether confirmed.json covers it (tools/checkrec.py); the exit status is the same

reads: voice=, music=, sfx= or events= and lib= files

text: 3-bus mix, music ducks under the voice (duck=on: + SFX), −14 LUFS
a level hierarchy from one anchor (the narration, else the music): VMR per line, SFX classes, depth

commands.name: qa
commands.summary: QA of the final mix: silence, dropouts, pumping, clicks and the cue check; qa mix: a profile mix's level report.
commands.when: after mix, before mux

text: final-mix QA: silence, dropouts, pumping, clicks + cue check (+ qa mix) (exit 1 on fail);
a dropout, dip or click burst the score asks for: confirm it in the project's confirmed.json (the confirm? line)
the mix report of a profile mix: VMR per line, words at risk, SFX classes, depth (exit 1 on a hard miss)
where to put headphones on: the weakest line, the loudest hit, the biggest turn, the ending, the AAC risk, 6 s each
into out/listen/ (--gate: into that review page); --picture: spectrogram, lines, events, loudness and cuts on one axis

passes at it when the master's own rate is over it;
a keyframe every 2 s, BT.709, sound and subtitles copied; the size against each limit, the PSNR against the master;
